title: Place and delete a pending order
summary: Place a buy [[limit-order|limit]] below the current price with a stop loss and take profit, find it in the Trade tab, then delete it.

steps.text: Check you are on your demo account before you start.
In the Quotes tab, note the current ask for EUR/USD.
Tap EUR/USD and choose the option to trade.
Change the order type from market to buy limit.
Enter a price about 50 pips below the current ask. If the app rejects it, check that the price is below the ask and not too close to it.
Enter a stop loss below your limit price and a take profit above it.
Place the order. Open the Trade tab and find it in the list of pending orders, separate from open positions.
Tap or press and hold the pending order (it depends on your app version), then choose the option to delete or cancel it.
Check the order has gone from the Trade tab.

afterQuestions.prompt: Why did your buy limit need a price below the current ask?

options.text: A buy limit aims to buy cheaper than now
options.explanation: Right: buy limits sit below the price; buy stops sit above it.

options.text: All pending orders must be below the price
options.explanation: No: sell limits and buy stops sit above the current price.

afterQuestions.prompt: While your pending order waited, did it show a profit or loss as an open trade?

options.text: Yes, it counted as an open trade
options.explanation: No: until it triggers there is no position, so there is no profit or loss yet.

options.text: No, nothing is open until it triggers
options.explanation: Right: a pending order only becomes a position if price reaches its level, so it has no profit or loss until then. Margin for pending orders is usually zero, but some brokers reserve some; check your broker's contract specification.
